name: Helon
overview: Helon was a male member of the tribe of Zebulun, noted in Scripture primarily as the father of Eliab. His mention is brief but specific, grounding him within the genealogical records of Israel. No additional personal notes or distinctions are provided beyond his paternal role.
namesAndTitles: The name Helon means 'strength' or 'power,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name with a strong, positive connotation. This meaning may imply qualities valued in his lineage or tribe, though the name was not given by God according to the record.
familyAndRelationships: Helon is explicitly identified as a descendant of the tribe of Zebulun and as the father of Eliab. Scripture does not record any other family relationships for him beyond these connections.
scriptureSignificance: Helon's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his role as a tribal ancestor within Israel, specifically as the father of Eliab, who is listed among the leaders of Zebulun. This genealogical detail contributes to the broader understanding of the tribal organization and leadership during the wilderness period. While his mention is brief, it anchors the lineage of Zebulun in the census records, underscoring the importance of family lines in God's covenant people.
